editorial:
Imagine waking up in 1915 Vancouver and finding out the police have set a trap just to ruin your life. You follow Dalip Singh and Naina Singh, two Sikh men working in the mills who get tricked by undercover cops into a fake romance. The whole thing is a setup to accuse them of sodomy and kick them out of Canada. It is not your typical history lesson because the movie switches styles constantly. One minute you are watching a serious drama, then it jumps into a documentary, and suddenly there are musical numbers. It feels like a wild ride that shows how racism and hate worked together back then to keep people of color down.

What really hits home is how the movie shows the unfairness of the legal system. The acting is great, and the mix of styles keeps you from getting bored, though the jumping between genres might feel a bit jumpy at first. You should definitely watch this if you like true stories about fighting for justice. Since it is an older indie project, your best bet is finding a high-quality digital copy. If you can find it to stream in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video or rent it on Apple TV, go for it. Otherwise, adding the Blu-ray to your physical collection is a great way to support this kind of art.
endingExplained: The film ends by showing how the legal system failed Dalip and Naina. Even though the evidence was fake and the cops lied, the men were still targeted because of who they were. It wraps up by connecting these old events to modern struggles for equality. You see that while the men suffered, their story serves as a warning about how power can be abused to destroy innocent lives just to keep a city white.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves true stories about social justice and unique filmmaking styles.
